worked_solution:
The straight-line solutions of the system have the form

$$
{c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069584/assets/1f166fad96cd30dbc0b9cf05fdabcccd26cd68e25fc26b91ae357d4015813614.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{away from the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{1}>0.$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069584/assets/cbb8268b959a09af3d0b57573ff08f45a2fb87f376d87f284df49cd5094412d9.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing $\text{toward the origin},$ meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must approach $\text{the origin}$ as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{2}<0.$
